chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

God will not afflict our Shiites with four [characteristics] that He afflicts others with: that they are for unrighteousness, or that they beg with their palms, or that they are given in their backs, or that they are greenish-blue [eyed].

key_terms.أَدْبَارِهِمْ: Backs (specifically referring to the anus in this context)

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics that the Shiites will not suffer from according to al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to highlight the distinct moral and physical purity of the Shia community, asserting they are spared from four specific afflictions. These include devotion to unrighteousness, the humility of begging, the practice of anal intercourse (often interpreted as a sign of effeminacy or specific vice in classical exegesis), and the physical trait of having greenish-blue eyes, which was considered a mark of distinction or specific lineage in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia.
